I got this router in anticipation of my two young girls growing into teenagers. The internet is an integral part of their educational and social life, so it's imperative to have good coverage throughout the house to reduce family stress.

The system consists of a router and two satellite signal boosters that you can use to ensure great internet throughout your home. As you can see from the pictures, the router has two gigabit ethernet ports. The satellites have a power plug and a sync button.

Every component is highly compact at 4.1 by 4.1 by 2.7 inches. There is also an app that allows you to have convenient control options on your phone. You also receive a 2 meter ethernet cable and three power adapters for the router and satellites.

The router and satellites are easy to hook up and sync. You can place them strategically throughout your home to ensure you get great internet coverage everywhere. I always make everyone in my family use their wi-fi on their phone rather than a data plan, so by reducing poor connectivity zones this router will definitely be a long term savings. I also like the compact size and design of all three elements. This is a great system for getting the most out of your internet.

all the basic controls are here in-line and work smoothly. Pairing was, as always between Apple products, fast and effortless. Immediately paired with all our phones/iPads fine.

call quality was good, microphone worked great.

they click together magnetically, but the wiring isn't super flexible, so I don't feel comfortable storing them in a small space. They come with 4 eartips for sizing.

As always with Apple, packaging was nicely minimal

I got these either for myself to have a pair of cheap earbuds to take places I don't want to have to worry about losing or to send to my son at college so he doesn't have to worry about losing them. They're budget earbuds but still fine sound, just not as good as the high-end ones, as should be expected. excellent product for its niche

text_fidelity_a:
Belkin N150 Wireless USB Adapter with up to 150Mbps Link Rate We have several networked devices in our house and also several individualized networks configured. Not all of the networks can be seen by all devices so I looked to this Belkin USB WiFi adapter to allow one of the older computer systems to access the most reliable network in the house - a 5GHz network that only one or two of the systems can see.

Installation was a snap. I popped in the CD, told it to install the drivers and we were off to the races. The particular target system was a 32-bit Windows Vista laptop. After just a couple of minutes the driver was completely installed and when I plugged in the USB adapter is was picked up immediately. I could see the desired network as well as several other networks in the neighborhood that were previously invisible to the computer. I shut off the built-in adapter, connected to the 5GHz network and went to the net.

So far, the connection has been very stable and speeds have been excellent. The router to which it is connected is a TP-Link router and so far we have seen no issues between the two devices. I have not had this adapter very long so it is still early to say it’s completely stable but all indicators up to this point have been very favorable.

Several other reviewers have mentioned that this adapter does not work with Linux. This is true - there are no drivers available for this adapter other than for Windows XP/Vista/7/8. If you need an adapter that will allow you to connect a Linux or Mac system to a wireless network, this is not the device you need right now.

So far I can’t find too much about which to complain concerning this router. It seems to be stable and reliable on the system to which it is attached here. I am satisfied with it and based on my experience with it can recommend it - if you’re sticking with Windows.
text_fidelity_b: Belkin N150 Wireless USB Adapter with up to 150Mbps Link Rate

text_fidelity_a:
museeq Bluetooth Speaker,Portable Wireless Conference Speakerphone Speaker,Waterproof Shower Speaker,Enhanced Bass,Stereo Sound,Shockproof,Dustproof Outdoor Speaker with Powerbank Black Bottom Line - The speaker itself is excellent but Bluetooth can be an irritating technology.

The speaker is lightweight and even has an attached carrying strap. Unlike a lot of lightweight products though, it doesn't feel flimsy or fragile at all. Instead it has a nice, solid, durable feel to it. While I am not an audiophile, the speaker has a deep, rich sound that I really like. It does well with audiobooks, music, and videos.

The problems seem to be with Bluetooth. One major issue is that the sound stutters while using Bluetooth. It's very noticeable when playing music and very irritating when listening to audiobooks. That's happened with every Bluetooth speaker I've ever tried. A google search indicates that it's a common problem related to the amount of information the computer is trying to pump out to the speaker. There's a checklist of possible issues to go through to try to fix the problem but the stuttering seems all too common with this technology.

Another issue involves changing modes on a Bluetooth speaker. To sidestep the stuttering I plugged this speaker into my computer with a standard jack. It worked fine and the sound was good. When I unplugged it to bring the speaker into another room with me, I had to redo my audio settings. When I plugged it back in with the jack, an audiobook played just fine but there was no sound while playing videos. Again, I had to go into the audio settings and fiddle with them to be able to watch a movie. I've had similar issues with other Bluetooth speakers.

If you are a techie you may be able to resolve such things quickly and easily. The less tech adept you are, the more hassle they will be though. Myself, I'm just going to leave the speaker connected to my pc via a good old fashioned jack because I like its sound. Bluetooth? Bah, I haven't got time to bother with it.
text_fidelity_b: museeq Bluetooth Speaker,Portable Wireless Conference Speakerphone Speaker,Waterproof Shower Speaker,Enhanced Bass,Stereo Sound,Shockproof,Dustproof Outdoor Speaker with Powerbank Black

ASUS VS197D-P 18.5" WXGA 1366x768 VGA Back-lit LED Monitor, Black I'm very pleased with this monitor. I needed to replace my second screen and didn't want to spend a lot, but needed a monitor with 1920x1200 resolution. This seemed like a decent bet. It has exceeded my expectations with regard to performance. The clarity is excellent -- it rivals my primary screen which cost three times as much!

The monitor is very lightweight. It comes with both DVI and VGA cables, which was unexpected. I like that there's no power transformer or wall wart. It has just a regular power cord. Set up is simple (just attached the base and no tools are needed).

Of course, at this price point some features are not present. For example, while the screen can be tilted back and forth a bit, it does not have any up/down adjustment, nor can it be swiveled into portrait mode. There's no USB connectors and no speakers. But for me, none of those were deal breakers. I wanted a good quality monitor that was affordable, and this hit the mark 100%. Plus, it does not scrimp on connections. There's DVI, VGA and HDMI. I'm using DVI at present since the PC I'm using it with is a few years old. But, my next PC will probably have a HDMI connection, making this monitor future-proof (well, as future-proof as any tech product can be).

If you're looking for a basic monitor that does not scrimp on image quality, this should definitely be on your short list. Also, check Amazon Warehouse for used ones. I got mine there (it was probably a customer's return). It looks brand new, and only ran me $127.

Sony X800H 55-inch TV: 4K Ultra HD Smart LED TV with HDR and Alexa Compatibility - 2020 Model Background: I spec and integrate the highest resolution LCD’s produced in aerospace defense applications. LCD image performance is measured in hundreds of dimensions and environments. Sony is not a player in that space.

For home, I’ve been SID show and showroom shopping LCD, OLEDs, etc image quality for years. This year, I’m replacing a comparably sized exercise room 1080p LCD set. Sony has always been, to my eye, a superb comparative model and a $100 or so more than other competitors. Is the premium worth it?

This Sony X800H is an eye grabber across the showroom and on close inspection. It’s a phenomenal picture. Sony’s proprietary LCD foundries are unique in the industry. The Sony LCD foundry produces a distinctive LCD that is worth the premium price to the discerning.

Performance-wise, Sony reduced the native refresh rate to 60hz from 120hz last year. That’s quite practical as it will be some years before >60fps cameras are widely available at native 120fps. No matter, the 60hz to 120hz refresh is not discernible to the eye. The X800H imaging software can be seen to take care of latency artifacts at factory default settings … no viewing distance ghosting, inverse ghosting, blur or pulse-width modulation.

There is a comment regarding darkness, edge lighting, and illumination issues. The X800H is both edge and background light as best as I can discern without tearing it apart. It's uniform lighting no matter. Sony has always been the master of the best 'optical black' pixel to enrich the color pixel perception. The X800H is loaded with image quality controls. Image software quality defaults arrived set at factory default. It was perfect out of the box. Don't adjust anything. I rarely futz with default settings. No one should have to. The vast majority of image problems are video source input. Change the channel first and compare the image.

An old school key attribute is viewing angles … how many degrees left/right and horizontal/vertical are necessary to degrade the image. The viewing angles here are excellent. Viewing angles are a peek into the remarkable quality of Sony’s proprietary LCD foundry.

Sony’s software, firmware, Smart integration, and image processors are likewise Sony proprietary. Sony names these features like everyone else. Feature comparisons are mostly apparent in year over year Sony tech evolution.

Of course, the real story is in the final image quality. The X800H is one excellent viewing experience.

Better than advertised. Better than expected. In this size, the X800H is the benchmark, IMHO.
text_fidelity_b: Sony X800H 55-inch TV: 4K Ultra HD Smart LED TV with HDR and Alexa Compatibility - 2020 Model

text_fidelity_a: Wireless Keyboard and Mouse Combo, Black Colorful Retro 2.4GHz Typewriter with Cute Round Keycaps, DPI Adjustable Optical Compatible PC Laptop First let me say that I grew up typing on actual typewriters and I find myself getting really nostalgic about those days the older I get.  Not that I mind sleek, modern keyboards.  I do a great deal of writing, so I have adapted to the various styles as they've come out.  This particular keyboard is nice and pleasant to work on, but I wouldn't say it's a true typewriter style experience.  The keys are too flat and too round for that.  If you are like me and you do a lot of typing and can adapt yourself quickly between different keyboards you will probably enjoy this one.  I do find myself making a lot of typos that I normally wouldn't when I'm working on it though.  The mouse is honestly just annoying.  There is no actual switch to turn it off, just a button right on top that seems to 'wake' it when it goes dormant, so if you're prone to bumping it around or accidentally dropping things on it or if you plan on using it in multiple places for any reason whatsoever you will find yourself getting frustrated with just how easy it is to turn it back on.  The scroll wheel is fantastic, but the one on my previous mouse no longer works at all, so that might be the reason why I like it so much.  The accuracy of its tracking leaves a lot to be desired and it's quite loud when you click it, but I do tend to prefer to keep my environment quiet.  All in all I would not purchase this again both because the keyboard design is just 'off' in enough nit-picky ways to make it frustrating (so many typos) and because the mouse tracking and lack of a true 'off' switch makes it frustrating to actually use it.  Both the keyboard and the mouse are really pretty to look at and well built for what they are, but I wouldn't call them truly functional even though they do work.  If you're just doing minor browsing and not a lot of typing they would be fine for that, but if you're someone that does a lot of writing or anything that requires precision tracking of the mouse like playing games or working in paint programs you should probably skip this set.
text_fidelity_b: Wireless Keyboard and Mouse Combo, Black Colorful Retro 2.4GHz Typewriter with Cute Round Keycaps, DPI Adjustable Optical Compatible PC Laptop

text_fidelity_a:
Harman Kardon Allure Voice-Activated Home Speaker with Alexa, Black As an avid fan of Alexa, I am delighted to have this Harman Kardon Alexa speaker. I've had my original Echo since the first week they released the initial invitation to buy and have since added a Dot and Alexa controlled thermostats, dining room lights, Fire TV sticks and plugs through out the house. This unit was meant to enhance the music sound quality from Alexa and expand our Alexa listening group and work with the living room television.

The speaker itself is considerably larger than my original Echo - wider and heavier. The lights on this are brighter as well - when playing music at night or listening to a book, you can leave the light on and it works as a night light. You can also turn the light off if you prefer. Setting this up takes a bit longer than my Echo or Dot - it's slower making the initial WiFi connection, but once you link to Amazon via the Alexa App, you're good to go. It connects via Bluetooth to both my LG V10 phone and my Samsung tablets without drama.

This unit is significantly louder at every volume setting than the original Echo and makes the Dot sound like she's whispering. I have this in our formal living room where we have 30 feet tall ceilings, grass cloth covered walls and an enormous open space - the room was designed for correct accoustics with my Grandmother's grand piano and music simply sounds beautiful in here. The Harman Kardon Alexa sits on a table where the piano used to be and the sound at volume 4 simply envelopes you no matter where you are in the room. Set the volume to 6 and I can hear my book or music two rooms away almost as if it's floating through the halls. The sound quality is excellent and playing Beethoven or opera or country music renders each instrument precisely from tiny flutes to cellos and twangy fiddles. I'm immensely pleased at the improvement from the Echo to this for just music.

The reason for the one star deduction is because I thought/expected the Harman Kardon to by fully, 100% integrated with Alexa. It is not. This unit cannot be linked to the Fire TV sticks, meaning that I cannot use it to verbally control the living room television. It cannot be linked to my Echo and Dot units. That means we can't include the Harman Kardon speaker in our multi room group so the same song/book can be heard throughout the house. We cannot do the Drop In skill where Alexa acts as an intercom system for multiple rooms. There are a couple of other skills this speaker isn't able to perform simply because it doesn't speak to the Amazon Alexa products. If they can correct this glaring deficiency, then this would be a five star product and one i would consider buying for the guest suite and master bedroom. As a stand alone Alexa unit, this is a top notch choice, but if you want to link to your existing Echo, you can't do so.
text_fidelity_b: Harman Kardon Allure Voice-Activated Home Speaker with Alexa, Black

text_fidelity_a:
Anker Roav SmartCharge F0 Bluetooth FM Transmitter for Car, Audio Adapter and Receiver, Hands-Free Calling, MP3 Car Charger with 2 USB Ports, PowerIQ, and AUX Output (No Dedicated App) I had no idea something like this existed until I saw it on one of those "Best Things I Ever Bought on Amazon" lists. I had Bluetooth in my old car, and I miss it. My husband's car doesn't have Bluetooth or, at least, it didn't. It does now, and it's so easy to set up! You simply plug this into your car's cigarette lighter, and it automatically finds the radio station that will work the best, depending on your location. You switch over to that station, and boom, connected! You'll even get a man's voice when you turn your car on telling you "waiting for connection," and then "successfully paired" once it syncs up, which doesn't take long at all.

CONS:
You have to leave the car on that radio station all the time for the Bluetooth to work, so this is better if you don't rely on scanning the radio much for car entertainment and use your phone for music more often. You also have to search for a phone number on your phone itself, so it's not ideal for calling people while driving unless you make the phone call first.

PROS:
There are two USB charger ports, so you can charge two phones at the same time (or two devices that use USBs). And here's an added bonus - the charger is turbocharged! I charged my phone from 14% to 65% in a 20-minute trip - excellent! Also, I was listening to an audio book on and off, and every time I turned the car on, the volume remained the same for the audio book - I didn't have to fiddle with it at all.

I didn't even know adding Bluetooth to your car was this easy. I thought I'd have to pay $300 for a mechanic to install it, so I put it off as something I just can't have in my husband's car. But this device makes it an almost seamless experience. The only true caveat I have with it is that I have to load up a phone number to call before I drive, but other than that, you just can't beat this little device for such a low price!

text_fidelity_a:
Arteck Wireless Solar Keyboard Full Size Solar Recharging Keyboard for Computer/Desktop/PC/Laptop/Surface/Smart TV and Windows 10/8 / 7 / Vista/XP Built in Rechargeable Battery I selected this keyboard after doing a bit of research. I already have a solar keyboard (a Logitech) on my Windows system, and I needed a keyboard for my Linux system. I was a little hesitant to buy because I did not see any definitive information that it would work with Linux. I've had it several days, and I can say with some authority, it definitely works correctly under Linux.

The system in question is a Dell laptop running Peppermint Linux hosting a CentOS 8 VM. Most keyboards (with one notable exception) work on this system so I was hopeful it would work well, and it does. It behaves virtually identically to the Logitech keyboard and so far has given me no trouble.

Build-wise, this is a solid keyboard that should hold up to some abuse. It is sturdy and does not flex when I am typing. I like the fact that the dongle is held to the back of the keyboard magnetically so it can be transported with less concern of being misplaced when not in use.

One of the major issues I have with keyboards is that I have the hands of a gorilla and I frequently run into issues with hitting multiple keys at the same time, particularly with flat keyboards like this one. The keys are slightly bigger than average with this one, though, and hitting muliple keys simultaneously is less of a problem. This was an unexpected and welcome surprise.

Aesthetically, I love the feel of this keyboard. Most of the keys are concave and feel pleasant to the touch. Oddly, a good number of the keys on the bottom row are actually convex. While this is no issue at all, I do find it puzzling.

It is priced competitively against the Logitech too.

If I could change anything I would include some kind of indicator of how much charge this keyboard has at any given time. So far I have not run out of power, but eventually I expect to have a situation where there has not been enough light to keep it at a full charge and it would be good to know how much power it has retained.

I'm pleased with this keyboard. It works well under Linux and I don't need to replace batteries or plug it in. I really can't ask for much more than that.
text_fidelity_b: Arteck Wireless Solar Keyboard Full Size Solar Recharging Keyboard for Computer/Desktop/PC/Laptop/Surface/Smart TV and Windows 10/8 / 7 / Vista/XP Built in Rechargeable Battery

text_fidelity_a:
Sony ICF-506 Analog Tuning Portable FM/AM Radio, Black, 2.14 lb It is harder and harder to find any radio that has an AM radio band on it, let alone a really good one. It is also rather difficult to find a decent radio that is not digitally tuned and controlled. This radio is a good solid radio with both of the above features on it.

WHAT IS THIS RADIO LIKE?
This radio is a good solid radio. It has a slide switch under the tuning bar which has three settings - OFF, AM, and FM. On the right side are two dials. There is one with volume that goes from Minimum to Maximum. The other dial is the tuning dial. That makes the tuning bar slide up and down for both AM and FM. There is a handle on top that flips up or goes down. There is a pull out telescopic antenna on the top for better reception. There is a place in the left side where you plug in the electric cord, but you can remove it if you prefer to operate solely by batteries. The cord is a little over 5 feet long. The plug is a two pronged plug and is polarized. There is a door on the back which slides off and allows you to put in 3 AA batteries. The door has attached hinges so you don't have to worry about losing the battery door off of the unit unless it breaks.

HOW DOES THIS RADIO PERFORM?
For AM I would say that it has okay reception It is not WOW but it is not terrible either. Since AM is not really dominating the airwaves anymore, I imagine that some people would not find this to be a problem. If you want really strong AM reception, this is okay, but you might be able to find better.

For FM reception, the radio is great. It pulls in quite a few stations and also plays them very clearly. The speaker is best showcased by FM. It is a full sound and impressive considering the size of the speaker and the basic nature of the radio. I found that it is a nice sound and enjoyable.

HANDLE
The handle has a bit of a recoil to help it snap back into place, but it does seem just a little bit flimsy to me. I wish it was just a bit sturdier. It is not enough to take off a star.

WHAT WOULD THIS RADIO COME IN HANDY FOR?
For those of you who are from the era where radios of this nature were commonplace, I am not writing this comment section for you. You already know what this would be good for. For those of you who think that In Tune, or other internet radio stations would suffice for any AM or FM radio stations, I would like to mention that during weather crises, that AM/FM and shortwave radio tend to be the only reception you can get if any. That includes disasters. At that point, internet is not an option, so it is important to have a back up communication capability to keep up on what is going on and any emergency information that might come up, or even information about upcoming help.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This radio is handy. It is a decent size, sturdy, and a solid basic radio. It gets decent reception and has a nice speaker which is especially nice for FM. During emergencies and times of crises, this is a good backup to have should internet not be an option. Running on both electricity and AA batteries, this would be a great addition to your basic emergency kit.

MY RATING
Despite the handle being a bit flimsier than I would like, it is still decent and a solid radio. I do not think that it is worth taking off a star.
text_fidelity_b: Sony ICF-506 Analog Tuning Portable FM/AM Radio, Black, 2.14 lb

text_fidelity_a:
Stellar Labs,Outdoor FM Antenna OMNIDIRECTIONAL 9/12/2015
Final Review:
Have now completed the installation and hookup of this antenna. The first test was to listen to Mixed Bag, 90.7 FM which was always full of static. Now this station comes in crystal clear, loud, and strong. Note that I decided to mount this antenna on the side of my house, just beneath the peak of my low roof facing the back yard. I had a quantity of twin 300 ohm cable which I wanted to use. Using a 300ohm/75ohm converter, I simply attached the end of the cable to the two 300ohm screws, protecting the connection with electrical tape. I measured and fabricated a wood mounting plate (see photo) and then screwed the mast bracket to it from the back. The wooden support board was then lag screwed, in turn, to the outside of my house just below the peak using 5" long screws. I then installed the antenna and mast, after reversing it. It now extends upwards vertically yet does not interfere with the roof line. The versatility of the mast permitted me to accomplish that.

(This review is preliminary. I assembled the antenna but am not yet ready to install it.
Assembly tips:

- Both curved antenna segments are secured to the antenna cross bar with the supplied hardware.
- The ends of one (bottom) segment are held in place with two phillips head screws. First, remove the curved metal clamp. line up the holes in the segment and, maintaining hand pressure on each segment end to ensure that it is seated firmly into it's curved metal seat, insert each screw and secure. Do not over tighten these fasteners. This is the "bottom" of the antenna, opposite the 75 ohm connector side. Attach one leg of the segment at a time.
- The ends of the second (top) segment are held in place with two hex head nuts. You will note that each nut is topped with a rubber 'O' ring. This is used to keep the nuts from threading off until assembly. Do not attempt to re-use these as they are not spacers or washers.
- Again, seat the ends of the antenna segment firmly in place, aligning the holes over the studs. Holding down the segment, install each nut. Do not over tighten these nuts.
- The closed loop ends of each antenna segment may now be gently guided in front of the black plastic locking clips. Once the looped ends are in position, firmly, yet carefully snap them into place. The circular antenna shape has now been completed. If assembled patiently and slowly, damage should not occur to the antenna.)
text_fidelity_b: Stellar Labs,Outdoor FM Antenna OMNIDIRECTIONAL

I figured the "lifetime map updates" feature would ensure this GPS shows the latest road closures to get me through the city without trouble. WRONG.

I HATE this GPS. I only gave it 2 stars because I like the graphics options and it lets you take screen shots of the map. If it WORKED properly, I'd say it could have been a great GPS, but it doesn't do what it promised.

SABRE Home Security Personal Safety Kit, Comes With A 120 dB Doorstop Alarm, 120 dB Door Or Window Alarm And A 120 dB Personal Alarm, Safety Essentials For College Students, Home Owners and Travelers For an apartment with only one door and one window that opens this set is great. But most places need a few more. For a dorm room this is fine. I've only seen dorm rooms that had one door and usually the dorm rooms windows are several stories up so it would probably be pretty hard for someone to enter that way. Unless it's on the ground floor.

The door stop alarm is extremely LOUD. And it will not stop SCREAMING until it is physically switched off. This is the first of this type I have ever tried out. A few years ago I bought about 10 door stop alarms of another brand and they were also very loud. However, once the pressure plate was released back up they would stop screaming. I guess it's good that it continues to scream until you stop it. Especially in a dorm type living situation. Someone would eventually come to see what was the matter. It takes one 9 volt battery.

The window alarm is extremely simple to install and the double sided sticky tape that comes with it is very strong. I have several of these window alarms attached to various windows at my home. They aren't the loudest but they should get the job done of scaring off an unwanted intruder. It takes 4 LR44 button batteries.

The personal key chain alarm is o.k. It's got a loud scream that makes my ears ring. It takes a good tug to pull out the pin to activate it. The small LED light is better than no light at all but don't expect a bright beam. It will help you find your keys if you dropped them in the dark. I think along with a sincere scream for help and the personal alarm screaming as well, I would think most aggressors would give up and try for an easier target.......at least I would hope so. It takes 3 LR44 button batteries.
text_fidelity_b: SABRE Home Security Personal Safety Kit, Comes With A 120 dB Doorstop Alarm, 120 dB Door Or Window Alarm And A 120 dB Personal Alarm, Safety Essentials For College Students, Home Owners and Travelers

text_fidelity_a:
Sony BDP-S350 1080p Blu-Ray Disc Player I've had my Sony S350 Blu-Ray player for over a year now and here are my thoughts. The picture is completely amazing, even makes regular dvd's look better. I love that there's no more cords for picture and more cords for sound, just one HDMI cable and poof - high quality picture and surround sound.

A couple things to consider before buying your Blu-Ray player and subsequent Blu-Ray discs:
1. Blu-Ray will play your regular dvd's but if you have a regular dvd player (such as in your car) you cannot play Blu-Ray discs in it.

2. Patience is needed with this unit. After putting in a movie, especially if it is somewhat new, it could take 3-5 minutes to load. I am personally never in that much of a hurry to start the movie. While the movie is loading (a progress/status bar is provided on-screen) I can make popcorn, get the dogs situated, etc.

3. In conjunction with #2, the owner of this player must also be diligent about updating the firmware inside the player. I updated my player once last year (in November) and have noticed slower loads with current movies, so I plan to update it again next month (March). My guess is that it's good to update it 1-2 times per year.
What's involved in updating the firmware? I log onto a blu-ray firmware site, choose my model of player, then burn the update to a dvd disc. Place the disc in the player, it will read and update your firmware (took mine about 5-10 minutes as I remember). Afterward, your player will load movies more quickly.
Note: Loading never occurs during the movie, the only load-time that is experienced comes immediately after inserting the disc. Here's an example of the patience it takes to operate this blu-ray player:
Turn the player on - wait about 30 seconds for the unit to be able to receive or eject a disc (if you're trying to quickly eject a disc and run it back to the movie store, this can seem long!)
Insert disc and close - wait 3-5 minutes for movie menu to load

After that, you're set to go. For me, it's worth the wait and the trouble to keep it updated. I am quite sure that future models will require less patience and diligence, but for now this is the way it is. If you want extremely good quality with your movies, it's a wonderful addition to your home theater.
text_fidelity_b: Sony BDP-S350 1080p Blu-Ray Disc Player

text_fidelity_a:
Acer Aspire One Cloudbook, 11-Inch HD, 32GB, Windows 10, Gray (AO1-131-C9PM) includes Office 365 Personal – 1 year **Discontinued by Manufacturer** There's a lot of reviews already about this product. I wavered for a good while about deciding if I wanted to accept this Cloudbook for review and now kind of wish I hadn't. As far as I'm concerned, the Cloudbook is like a merging of a laptop and a chromebook with neither giving the features that are special to each one. As far as it being a computer, it runs on Windows 10 of which I have great suspicions and doubts. If you remember, I believe most everyone received an offer for a free download of Windows 10 as an upgrade from whatever Windows program they were currently using. I have read from several sources that it was offered only as a way of installing NSA spyware on your computer. We are being watched and monitored at every turn. If you don't believe me, next time you are driving take a look at all the cameras on poles along the roads and highways and tell me we aren't being surveilled. Smartphones, smart TV's, smart refrigerators, dryers and washing machines are simply ways of letting TPTB know what we are doing at all times. How many loads of clothes you washed, what you are doing in your bedroom and on and on. So, what does all this have to do with this little and cute computer? It has Windows 10 installed.

If you are o.k. with that then overall it's not a bad machine. I really miss having a disk drive to load my own personal programs and don't like having to download stuff from the internet via the app store or some other internet source. And since it is a computer but has very little space for storage, you have to have an anti-virus program. It comes with one but it's only good for 30 days and you have to purchase it or get another one. Most of your stuff will be stored in the Cloud (like a chromebook) unless you opt for a Sandisk or external hard drive. And if you buy an external hard drive for more storage why not get a regular computer instead that has more bells and whistles and possibly a disk drive?

It looks like a chromebook and I have had to put a label on it to distinguish it from mine and my kids chromebooks. I'm having a hard time getting used to Windows 10 and it takes a long time to finally get on the internet. I have taped a piece of paper over the camera lens staring me in the face - call me paranoid if you wish but I don't like people in my house uninvited. The "shift" key is way too small and I'm always missing it.

As far as specs go they're listed on the main page but here they are again for your convenience:

11.6" HD Widescreen ComfyView LED-backlit Display (1366 x 768 resolution, 16:9 aspect ratio).
Intel Celeron N3050 Dual-Core Processor 1.6GHz with Intel Burst Technology up to 2.16GHz.
Windows 10
Intel HD Graphics
2GB of DDR3L Onboard Memory.
32GB Internal Storage
Secure Digital (SD) card reader.
802.11ac WiFi (Dual-Band 2.4GHz and 5GHz).
Bluetooth 4.0
Webcam (640 x 480)
High-definition audio support.
Two Built-in Stereo Speakers.
1 - USB 3.0 port
1 - USB 2.0 port
1 - HDMI Port with HDCP support.
Microsoft Office 365 Personal 1-Year Subscription (activation code included).
2-cell Li-polymer battery pack (4200mAh).
Up to 8 hours of battery life (Video Playback).
2.54 lbs. | 1.15kg (system unit only).

If you are already using Windows 10 then it should be easy to navigate, but I feel as if I'm learning a whole new OS though I use Windows 8 on my other laptop. It only detected two of my Bluetooth devices and I have several. If you want Word processing you must redeem your card number inside the box before a certain date or else it expires. And it's all cloud based so your data is out there and not in your pc safe and sound.

I will modify this review as needed, but I have not used this computer since a few days ago and probably will not be using it much at all. I like my chromebook better for web surfing, and it doesn't require an anti-virus program because it's totally cloud based but I never use the cloud. I store the stuff I want on my old desktop or other laptop. And my chromebook has access to a word processing program without having to buy it.
text_fidelity_b: Acer Aspire One Cloudbook, 11-Inch HD, 32GB, Windows 10, Gray (AO1-131-C9PM) includes Office 365 Personal – 1 year **Discontinued by Manufacturer**

text_fidelity_a: Dericam PTZ WiFi IP Security Camera,1080P Surveillance CCTV Outdoor Camera, Pan/Tilt/Zoom, 4X Optical Zoom, Night Vision, Motion Detection, IP65Weatherproof Pre-Installed 32G SD Card, Black I got two outdoor security cameras of different brands at the same time.  The other brand I could not get to work and setting it up was complicated and could apparently only be done through a cell phone.  This camera, on the other hand, could be set up with a computer and the setup was easy and I had it working within minutes, for a live feed.  The picture quality is good and I tested in the dark and still got a great picture.  I didn't give it 5 stars because I couldn't get it to record (supposedly it has some built-in memory, although you can also add a memory card for more memory).  For ease of setup and for the live feed, I give it 5 stars.  I'll try to work with it some more and if I get all the features working, will update this review.  Important note:  I got this without giving thought to the fact that I didn't have a good place to mount it outside.  Also, it needs an outlet to be plugged into, as do most security cameras.  I have outside outlets, but nothing up near the roof where I would want to mount this.  The power cord is not long enough to go for a very great distance, so might require an extension cord to run it.  An exposed extension to a security camera is not very secure, as all anyone would need to do is unplug it to disable the camera.  I thought perhaps I could just keep it inside and aim it out of a window.  Unfortunately my windows sills are two narrow for the camera to sit and shoot out of a window.  I didn't find a good way yet to mount in front of a windows.  Of course my lack of planning is no fault of the camera.  The camera seems rugged and well built.  It appears to be able to use 5Ghz Wi-Fi; the other camera I tested did not.  There is one slight design flaw; the aerial is very close to the mounting bracket, so it is difficult to position it properly.
text_fidelity_b: Dericam PTZ WiFi IP Security Camera,1080P Surveillance CCTV Outdoor Camera, Pan/Tilt/Zoom, 4X Optical Zoom, Night Vision, Motion Detection, IP65Weatherproof Pre-Installed 32G SD Card, Black

text_fidelity_a:
ASUS MeMO Pad FHD 10 ME302C-A1-BL 10.1-Inch 16GB Tablet (Blue) I've used a Chromebook, I've used various Kindles, but this is my first experience with a tablet. The Android OS is still pretty alien to me, and I'm still knocking around in it, discovering how it works. So it's probably not fair to review the tablet itself based on my own inexperience with the OS. But this tablet is high resolution, easy on the eyes, and amply large. I love that it senses the ambient lighting and adjusts automatically, because my Kindles don't do that and I have to take the brightness up and down manually.

One thing I don't like about it is that it does not use Flash so you can't play anything that requires Flash. Any attempts to add Flash give you messages that Google or Adobe have decommissioned Flash and will not use it. I spent several hours nosing around in the forums looking for a solution, and even found some cautions that I could hurt my tablet by trying to install a Flash player, so I didn't do it. Sure, geeks and power users may laugh at this, but I don't want to mess with it. But what this means is that I cannot watch Amazon Prime movies on this tablet, which is a real bummer. In the forums I found discussions about this; it's apparently a problem with Amazon, not anybody else. They have not developed an app to allow playing their instant videos on Android systems. Somebody said they were hoping an app would be out by 2014, but that there was no guarantee; that Amazon is probably trying to protect its Kindle market by not releasing an app. So my normally high estimation of Amazon is knocked down a peg for absence of an app. Hopefully they will rememdy this soon.

The first thing I did was order a rooCase for it, but I discovered that the cut-out in the rooCase for the rear-facing camera vignetted photos and videos (imagine a black circle around the edges). So I took the plunge and ordered [[ASIN:B00BP54KNM ASUS Official Folio Keyboard Case for MeMOPad Smart ME301 Series]], and that's given me a completely different experience with this tablet. It feels more like my Chromebook, if a little less stable in my lap. I like the soft-touch ON button on the Folio keyboard case because, without it, it's kind of hard to turn on the tablet. There are a few Bluetooth connection issues with the Folio keyboard case, but that's for another review.

One thing that is weird to me about this tablet is that you are not supposed to leave it plugged in to the charger. I'm used to leaving my Kindles plugged in overnight, but with the Asus tablet you're only supposed to leave it plugged in for eight hours at most. (And if you get the Folio keyboard case for it, you use the same charger for both, one after the other.) The screen is more responsive to touch than my Kindle Fire, but still there is sometimes a lag that I haven't quite gotten used to yet. I think it's like learning to drive a new car: you just have to get used to the way it handles, and then you can groove right on into it.

It is definitely easier on the eyes than a 7" screen. Again, the auto-adjusting brightness is a major boon. I love that I can pick it up in the middle of the night, read or browse for a while, then close it up in its case (which auto-offs) and go back to sleep. I'm still not sure I'm in love with the whole tablet concept, but Google Voice definitely makes it easier to use it. For the money, I think this Asus offering is a very good value.
text_fidelity_b: ASUS MeMO Pad FHD 10 ME302C-A1-BL 10.1-Inch 16GB Tablet (Blue)

TP-Link AC1750 Wireless Dual Band PCI-Express Adapter (Archer T8E) Wow! What an improvement this internal TP-LINK ARCHER T8E DUAL BAND PCI EXPRESS ADAPTER makes over the quite satisfactory external [[ASIN:B007ZLGXA8 Linksys AE3000 dual band adapter]] that I've used since October 2012. Internet pages load much faster (on both the 2.4GHz and 5GHz bands), and the wireless signal is stronger (5 bars, not 4). My router is located in a room far from my home office, and the adjustable external antennas help pull in the best signal.

The Archer T8E adapter is a breeze to install. Just open your computer's case, locate the PCI Express slot (the motherboard should identify it), insert the adapter, and close the case. Then use the included Resource CD to install the driver and utility. (The driver and utility can also be downloaded from the TP-Link web site.) The Resource CD also contains a detailed user guide in .pdf format. My CD arrived with a hairline crack (stuff happens!), but the software ran perfectly anyhow; and the adapter found and connected to my home wireless network without difficulty.

I really wish that I'd installed an internal wireless adapter a long time ago. So far, I'm delighted with the performance of this one.

text_fidelity_a:
Aokeo USB Microphone, Condenser Podcast Microphone for Computer. Suitable for Recording, Gaming, Desktop, Windows, Mac, YouTube, Streaming, Discord For the price this is a very nice USB microphone, I would agree with other reviewers that it performs on par with or better than similar competing USB condenser mics in this price range such as Blue Snowball or the Behringer C1.

I do wish it came with more accessories though similar to the non-USB version. The Aokeo AK-60 XLR version comes with a scissor boom arm, shock mount and pop filter for the same price.. so if you do happen to have a compatible audio interface with phantom power then I would recommend the XLR version.

The main annoyance with this mic is that when using it in windows 10 the driver does not have native mic gain control option. In many recording programs you can boost the mic gain via other means but if using this mic for gaming or other purposes through the native drivers then you will have to be very close to the mic to produce adequate volume (ie you pretty much need a boom arm) or otherwise you will need to boost gain via external passthrough program such as APO equalizer. I have also tried this mic in linux and the drivers there do have native gain control.

Overall I do think the sound quality and construction of the mic is good for the price and I would recommend it .. just note that if using windows 10 you will probably either need a boom arm or need to use external software to boost the mic gain. A boom arm is strongly recommended anyways to prevent extraneous noises like keyboard clacking, etc..
text_fidelity_b: Aokeo USB Microphone, Condenser Podcast Microphone for Computer. Suitable for Recording, Gaming, Desktop, Windows, Mac, YouTube, Streaming, Discord

I was a little concerned with the DIMMs as they were a little fatter than normal, but they snapped easily into my Dell desktop computer. Both Windows 7 and Ubuntu recognized the memory at once, with no issues, which really was to be expected.

Often, I'll run multiple VMs at a time. I do software development, so often I'll have one VM running Windows Server 2008, hosting SQL Server, while a second acts as a development box, and a third, which is frequently wiped out and recreated (or really, cloned from a blank copy) acts as a testing machine. Each of these machines gets 4 gig dedicated ram, and I leave the last 4 for the host OS. This RAM has held up to that kind of intense use without any problem. I am delighted.

I also use this machine for intense gaming, and again, this RAM does an awesome job. The memory, left at default configuration, is fast, fast, fast. Again, I'm a happy user.

Overall, I think the product is an exceptional value -- a top performer at a sensible price. The best I can say is, after a while you won't notice it. It will give you solid performance with no problems, and will just become invisible as you. I will definitely be using them again next time I'm in the market for memory.

text_fidelity_a:
Case Logic DCB-308 SLR Camera Sling (Black) I have been using this sling for some time now. When I received this sling I was seriously looking at buying the [[ASIN:B0036AWR8E Lowepro SlingShot 202 AW]] and I think for my purposes, this is the better sling for me. The one thing I did not like about the Lowpro was that it was broken up into two compartments which limited my ability to put my Canon 200-400 5.6 zoom in it comfortably. The large main compartment easily, but snugly holds my 40D and lense, which room to spare to include a wide angle.

As for slings in general. I have a Tamarac backpack which I love, but tend to way over pack (because I can.) It is bulky and awkward to wear, but does have a hip belt to take the weight off the shoulders. Also, I tried a holster style case, but it never felt secure and I never trusted my camera and lense in such a flimsy case. The sling, once in place seems to become a part of my body while hiking and climbing. It feels more secure than the backpack and far more secure than the holster.

Good Points

- nice spacious compartment for a DSLR and Zoom lense
- Sturdy with strap across you chest, it feels very secure on.
- Rotating the sling gives a sturdy platform to remove or insert camera.
- It is not big enough to overpack
- plenty of space for battery, charger, cards, notebook or guide, and two lenses and body
- Rain cover is nice addition (have not used it, but love the extra insurance.)
- Well padded
- Nice construction, classic design.
- Nice side handle for carrying when not slung.

Bad Points

- Sling Accentuates Man-boobs (I've tried several different ways of placing the strap, but it seems the only fix is portion control and moderate exercise.)
- no hip belt so weight is held on shoulders for long hikes, but weight is limited somewhat by size.

All in all, I have to admit I have come to love this sling. It has traveled with me quite a bit and I trust it to hold my treasured camera and lense. Easy to pack and will handle the essentials. It is cheaper than the Lowe sling in price, but not functionality. I recommend this to anyone who wants to pack in a DSLR.
text_fidelity_b: Case Logic DCB-308 SLR Camera Sling (Black)

Which fixed it. It needed to have the power cut completely in order to reset. Your mileage may vary, but for me, that's a nonstarter. Get it? The husband thinks it's no big deal, at least not worth replacing until it quits entirely. He's the installer, so he wins.

Three and a half stars.

HP 970 Programmable Wireless Keyboard (Silver) - Bluetooth & 2.4 GHz Wireless Multi-Device Connectivity - USB-C Rechargeable Battery - 24 Programmable Keys - Works with Windows & MacOS (3Z729AA#ABA) I got my first PC in 2003, and had a corded mouse. Looking back, I can BARELY remember the mouse that came with that Gateway PC. In 2004, my mom bought a Dell PC and traded me for my Gateway – don’t judge, she just wanted something to browse the internet and play games on.

Between 2003-2005, I used an awkward racecar shaped mouse, but went back to the more streamlined corded mouse for my desktops.

In 2005, when I got a laptop, I got my first wireless mouse and liked it. It was a Logitech.

By 2010, I got my first HP laptop – and as usual, got a specific mouse for it, again Logitech. The reason? My hand. I don’t have very big hands and hate to “splay” my fingers out trying to grip the mouse. That continued with a backup laptop in 2011 with some college money.

I even got “backup” mice, I just LOVED the Logitech ones.

Last year, 2021, I got another HP laptop for my birthday and yes – a “Logi” mouse (M317 – Amazon code B08L8SRJRR; white with purple/pink side grip, flowers on top). This was a bit smaller than my previous mice. But, I love it.

Thinking this might be a bit better – I got it.

Right off – it is a bit “extra”. I can BARELY grip it to get it to do what I need to do. The “thumb” rest was a good idea, the USB rechargeable feature was nice, programmable buttons – a bit beyond me. This is definitely for someone who needs those features.

As far as “quiet” with regards to the scrolling and clicking – I don’t see the need for the feature. When I’m typing on they keyboard that is noisier than my mouse.

It was response and fast – but not enough to justify a purchase of it.

It connects the same way my “Logi” does – USB dongle. Both mice take ONE (1) AA battery

At the current price of $67.52 – this is a definitely no-go for me.
text_fidelity_b: HP 970 Programmable Wireless Keyboard (Silver) - Bluetooth & 2.4 GHz Wireless Multi-Device Connectivity - USB-C Rechargeable Battery - 24 Programmable Keys - Works with Windows & MacOS (3Z729AA#ABA)

I’d say good price for the money and worth it for what I got!!! Just keep in mind the weight and size of your TV to ensure the proper support.

Kensington Pro Fit® Ergo Vertical Wireless Trackball (K75326WW), Black, 3" x 4" x 6.1" Initially, I liked the ergonomic design. It put much less pressure on my wrist than the Logitech trackball I've been using for many years. Unfortunately, when I started up World of Warcraft, I noticed the Kensington trackball button mapping software disabled the ability to use more than one button at once. I found the same detriment in Overwatch where multiple buttons often need to be pressed simultaneously. When I contacted the company, they sent me an email. The following is a direct quote from their email:
"Thank you for contacting Kensington Technical Support.

We would like to inform you that these trackballs are designed for basic office use and will not work on gaming applications.

We appreciate your time and patience."

To me, this came across as rather rude. This, coupled with the fact that this very mouse shows up in searches for gaming trackball mouse made me extremely disappointed and, in fact, somewhat angry. I feel Kensington needs to do any or all of the following. 1. Fix the software to make their hardware gaming inclusive. 2. Stop advertising their non-gaming devices as gaming devices (I feel this is blatant false advertising.) 3. Ask customers how they could fix issues rather than giving them a short, curt email to inform us that we, apparently, are idiots for expecting their devices to work as advertised.

Bottom line: I do not recommend buying this product unless all you intend to use it for is emails and youtube.

text_fidelity_a:
StarTech.com StarTech.com 1-Port 10/100 Mbps Parallel Network Print Server - Fast Centronics Ethernet Printer Server Adapter - Windows 10 (PM1115P2) Customer service is 6 stars

I certainly would love this product if we could have gotten it to work. I'm on a 5GB wifi network, and the StarTech is for a 2.4GB network. It won't work with my Internet speed. Or so both my techie, Brian, and I thought. Keep reading.

However... I couldn't connect the print server (that's the little white box) with my laptop. I had a problem and got online to get it fixed. The chat tech was very polite, patient and knowledgeable, but pointed me to the support page that gave me step by step how to set up my wifi print server. Went there. Followed the steps but I had no idea what the server IP address was. Gave up until I could call and get someone to walk me through it. A survey came up asking for my thoughts on my experience. I told them I was having a problem and just needed to know what my server IP address was so I could set up to print from my laptop. Got an email from a supervisor asking if I'd like a more experienced tech to call me. Yes! I would.

Got a call from Brian. He was very helpful, patient, and walked me through everything. Then I had to let him have remote control over the process because it got too complicated for me. That's when we discovered that the print server wouldn't work with my internet speed. So I told him how grateful I was for his patience and help even though I couldn't use the thing that was going to save me so much time. We hung up and while I was typing up this 6-star review of StarTech's great tech support, Brian called me back and said he was pretty sure he'd figured it out. I gave him remote control again, and 15 minutes later I've got my wonderful wifi printer!! I'm so elated! It works.

I have Windows 10 OS on my Dell Inspiron laptop, and an HP J4540 printer -- 2008. They are now friends and talking to each other wirelessly.

I do not recommend anyone that does not know what they are doing to install this device themselves. I know a lot about computers, but I know when I need an expert. Brian is an expert! Installing the thing is complicated. If your wifi is 2.4GB, then you can follow the instructions on the website most likely without a problem. If you have a higher speed Internet, then there's a lot more backdoor stuff that needs doing. I have a feeling they'll be updating the instructions on the website for this kind of problem. But if you have any problems, contact StarTech tech support. They are the greatest this side of the sun... no joke!
text_fidelity_b: StarTech.com StarTech.com 1-Port 10/100 Mbps Parallel Network Print Server - Fast Centronics Ethernet Printer Server Adapter - Windows 10 (PM1115P2)

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech MX Vertical Wireless Mouse – Advanced Ergonomic Design Reduces Muscle Strain, Control and Move Content Between 3 Windows and Apple Computers (Bluetooth or USB), Rechargeable, Graphite I have a couple of vertical mice that I use with my various computer systems, and they really do help with wrist fatigue and pressure. I also have a very nice Logitech MX Ergo trackball which is my go-to device for all of my systems. With Logitech releasing this vertical mouse, I was very optimistic that I would have the perfect solution. I was sorely disappointed. This is the worst Logitech device I have used and I can’t recommend it.

I’ll start with the good aspects of it, and then I will get into what isn’t so good.

This device can be connected via wireless USB or by Bluetooth. This is handy for when you want to use multiple systems and want to connect to them, in different ways. If you already have another wireless Logitech device, it can connect to the receiver for that device, reducing the number of wireless ports required. It connects well through either method and I have been able to move it between systems just with the press of the connection button on top.

In operation, it seems to work well as a pointing device. I will say that if you are not used to working with a vertical mouse there is a learning curve that is involved and you will be very frustrated while you make the adjustment. The movement isn’t hard – it’s working with the buttons which even though are worked with the same fingers they feel unnatural at first. This is a problem with all vertical mice, not just this one.

It is rechargeable, meaning no more batteries, and it holds a charge for a good while. I like mice and keyboards that don’t need batteries as in the very long term it saves money. (Logitech has a solar keyboard that is phenomenal and never needs to be plugged in at all – great device.)

I have three main issues with this vertical mouse. The first is the build quality. It feels very lightweight and cheap, and I would call it fragile. It is supposed to be light and maneuverable so it’s easy to use, but it’s so much so that it has a very cheap feel to it that is unsettling. Second, this is a HUGE mouse which for me is great but for most people is unworkable. It fits my hand very well, but I have hands like a gorilla. My wife tried it and found it to be completely unusable because she couldn’t work the buttons well at all due to the size. Finally, this is a very expensive peripheral compared to other vertical mice I have used that I actually prefer. This vertical mouse presently sells here for about $100. I have one that cost around $25 at the time I bought it, feels more solid and is easier to use. My wife and I compared the Logitech vertical mouse with my cheaper one, and we both agreed that the less expensive one was easier to handle and worked just as well. The only thing I lose with the cheaper mouse is Bluetooth connectivity, which in my case is not a deal breaker.

I wish I could rate this mouse more highly but I just can’t. It’s expensive, feels cheap and just isn’t made to fit smaller hands (and usually, it’s a challenge finding mice for larger hands). It’s worth consideration if you need a mouse that can be easily transitioned between wireless and Bluetooth, but if you just need to use it with one system I’d recommend researching other options before making a purchase.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech MX Vertical Wireless Mouse – Advanced Ergonomic Design Reduces Muscle Strain, Control and Move Content Between 3 Windows and Apple Computers (Bluetooth or USB), Rechargeable, Graphite

Jabra Stealth Bluetooth Headset - Black (US Version) I am pleased with this headset; the sound quality is good and audibility is very sharp. The music quality is also good. Assembly is very simple and needs no additional tools to set it together. It also fits well into my ears. I have been using this set for the last three weeks and it works great. It is paired with my cell phone and I use this to listen to the incoming calls and also listen to the music from micro SD card inserted into the cell phone. It is small and has a discreet design. It is very light, easy to carry and works great. The gadget also synchronizes easily with phone, but it does not pair with my Garmin Nuvi GPS machine or my Acer Chromebook both of which are Bluetooth-enabled.

Pairing with cell phone is very easy; just turn the headset on and the cell phone on, it detects the Bluetooth easily and within a minute it gives the message that it is paired. The built-in battery is excellent, and on one charge it lasts for about 5-6 hours of use time. The downside is that this piece doesn't have a separate mute button or the volume button; you have to control volume from your cell phone. Another negative feature is that the three replacement parts for earpiece that comes with the set are of same size, hence gives little option for someone with small (or large) ears. I have rated this product four stars for overall satisfaction.

I've tried to upgrade earbuds (nothing too pricey) and have always been disappointed.

🏋🏼‍♀️ I wear them while I work out. They have a great sound and block outside noise pretty well. They help me get in my zone in my own little world, and I love them.

💦 I tried to swim in them, and while they're waterproof, they stop playing as soon as my head is underwater.

🎧 The plastic ear tips, which are super comfortable for my tiny ear holes, eventually broke down — as aging plastic will do. I replaced them with BLLQ Replacement Ear Tips, which are nearly identical to the originals [[ASIN:B07FF9DN5K BLLQ Replacement Ear Tips]].

💵 They're $20. BT 4.1. So not the newest Bluetooth, and I'm sure Bose sounds better. But at this price point, I love these little guys.

🏆 Actually, I got them on a lightning sale for $13, so even better! So I paid $20 for the earbuds AND replacement tips.

🌚 I still want something new because I just want something new, you know. But knowing the disappointment I always feel with my attempted replacements, I'll probably keep using these sweet little babies.

🔊 I don't know what the heck they're talking about with the "noise canceling" in the product title. There is no ACTIVE noise-canceling, but the earbuds do form slight seals, which have a passive noise-canceling effect. I think I actually bought them for noise-canceling, but whatever. It's overrated as a feature unless you are willing to pay hundreds of dollars.

In sum, these are great earbuds, especially if you're prone to losing things and hate to feel heartbroken about losing something expensive.

text_fidelity_a:
EarStudio ES100 MK2-24bit Portable High-Resolution Bluetooth Receiver/USB DAC/Headphone Amp with LDAC, aptX HD, aptX, AAC (3.5mm Unbalanced & 2.5mm Balanced Output) Very nice features, sounds great, 2.5 balanced output! BT v5, aptXHD, top of the line DAC’s, great battery life. So why just 4 stars? The documentation leaves a lot to be desired. The included printed doc was about the size of a matchbook with writing so small it required a magnifying glass to read and for all that effort it basically said nothing. The biggest hassle was the pairing. It couldn’t be less intuitive. I have many BT devices, both receivers and transmitters and this is the first one that required a web search to figure out. Very frustrating. And to enable the BT v5 it requires a ROM flash upgrade so you have to connect it to a PC and follow a bunch of steps that are as intuitive as the pairing. I came within seconds of sending it back but stuck it out because it had some pretty stellar reviews. It turns out I’m glad I did. Once you get it sorted out it is a pretty amazing piece of kit. I use it with my HiBy r6 and BGVP DMG’S as well as my ATH M-50x headphones. I can now roam freely around the kitchen while keeping the DAP safely out of the way. I can plug-in the 2.5mm balanced cable and get outstanding sound with the added bonus of not heating up the DAP (it gets hot when plugged in directly) and the battery life of the HiBy is more than doubled. Both of these bonuses more than make up for the minor degradation in sound staging. I have listened for over 7 hours without the battery giving up, but have not used it up to it’s limit yet so I can’t say how long it will last. Is it worth the Benjamin it cost? Oh yeah.

Update: Upgraded to 5 stars after a month of use. Once the niggling little details were figured out and the unit was set up I can't say enough good things about this puppy. My main reason for getting a BT transmitter was I am going to be doing extensive bicycle touring later this year and since it will be solo touring I wanted good quality music available. I have an extensive library of 24 bit flac's as well as a couple of hundred audiobooks for the trip and while the playback of the books isn't important the music is. I invested a fair amount of cash into a HiBy R6 DAP and BGVP DMG IEM's as well as upgraded cables to connect them. The EarStudio lets me connect via 2.5" balanced with no real discernible degredation in the quality of the playback as opposed to plugging directly into the output on the DAP, and here's the kicker, instead of just getting 6 - 7 hours of playback and heating up the DAP I now get double that without any heat. I can stash the HiBy in a Pelican 1020 case and put it in my top tube bag where it's out of harms way and protected in case of misadventure. The EarStudio has a battery life of around 14 hours (I haven't run it out yet, and I have listened for over 8 hours). Added to that the App that is available for my Android based DAP is amazing. More fiddly bits than your above average geek could ever want. So I gotta give it a 5 star rating. And it's worth twicw the price but don't tell Radsone.
text_fidelity_b: EarStudio ES100 MK2-24bit Portable High-Resolution Bluetooth Receiver/USB DAC/Headphone Amp with LDAC, aptX HD, aptX, AAC (3.5mm Unbalanced & 2.5mm Balanced Output)

Michael Kors Men's & Women's Gen 6 44mm Touchscreen Smart Watch with Alexa Built-In, Fitness Tracker, Sleep Tracker, Heart Rate Monitor, GPS, Music Control, Smartphone Notifications I have used smart watches for a while now and I have seen a steady progression in the technology. This is my first Gen 6 watch. It is a big improvement from what I have used before (beyond just battery life) and so far I am pleased with it.

This is an Android-based smart watch, and it is similar in interface to previous smart watches I have seen and used. If you have used any generation of smart watch before this one the experience is very similar. I won't get too deep into the nuts and bolts of that or the WearOS app.

There are two big areas of improvement I have seen with this new watch. First, the battery life is much better than previous smart watches I have used which is very encouraging. I have a Gen 2 watch that I love but it lasts only about 3 days on a charge, and my Gen 5 is not much better. This one lasts several days before the battery runs out.

The more important improvement to me, though, is the way it doesn't interfere with the Bluetooth in my car. Previous watches messed up my ability to stream to the car's sound system to the point that the sound would sputter and simply die. I did trace it to the watch by powering off the watch completely after which the problem went away and would come back when the watch was powered on. This watch does not interfere at all and my car's Bluetooth works whether the watch is on or not.

This is a stylish watch, a bit more upscale than some of the others I have seen and used. The band is a non-stretch link band that is a little snug but not unworkable.

So far this watch works well for me. I am pleased with the improved battery life and even more happy that it doesn't mess with my car's Bluetooth connectivity.
text_fidelity_b: Michael Kors Men's & Women's Gen 6 44mm Touchscreen Smart Watch with Alexa Built-In, Fitness Tracker, Sleep Tracker, Heart Rate Monitor, GPS, Music Control, Smartphone Notifications

42 Inch/106CM Light Reflector 5-in-1 Collapsible Multi-Disc with Bag - Translucent, Silver, Gold, White and Black for Studio Photography Lighting and Outdoor Lighting I ordered the 43 Inch/110 Centimeter Light Reflector. It comes in it's own little zippered bag. The fabric appears to mostly be nylon, so it should wash easily with a damp cloth. The stitching is solid. I didn't know what to expect, but the Light Reflectors are exactly as pictured. My only little gripe is I had to refer to the listing to remember how to fold it to fit back into the pouch. Once you remove it, you have a large disk, silver on one side, black on the other. This has another zipper on the side. Inside the reflector's zipper is a diffuser which you will need to remove from the larger pouch to use. This is where the mounting tab is located. You will need the mounted clip that is available as part of the kit, or you may purchase it separately. That's not all. The large, outer pouch is reversible, so you then reverse the large pouch and you have a gold reflector one one side or a solid white on the opposite side. This is how you have black, white, gold, silver and a diffuser all in one. The diffuser has it's own tap to clip on your tripod, which pokes through from a button hole to mount the entire piece. You will need to make sure it's pulled through if you remove the outer layer of the reflector.

This is a good purchase for the value. I'm a hobbyist, and sometimes take photos of my projects. My problem comes from being a night-shift worker. I live and work at night. I must make my own lighting setup if I want to photograph anything at night, even in my home. It's light weight, and folds to a small circle, so this is also portable. It weighs less than a pair of jeans.

Here's a free tip: Only use the gold if your subject is brown. I don't find the gold reflector so useful. I'm glad it's available, but I doubt it will get much use for me. Also, place the reflector in a way that would mimic the sun's light, and your subject will look more natural. This is where the clips and extension arms from your tripod can come in handy if you are working solo. Of course, you can always enlist the assistance of another for outdoor shoots. Sometimes this is a best option if it's available. In the movies, they tend to show someone holding a reflector with it facing up towards the subject, but that's only because it does look silly holding a big disc over your head. If you hold it, you will need to hold it up over your head, and it will look silly but your photos will not.

It's a good tool to have on hand for any level of photography. I mostly photograph my doll collection. Once or twice a year, our doll collectors group will gather outdoors for shoots. We've not had a reflector available to us before, so this will help us immensely finding good spots to make photographs, even if the clouds are moving or we want to setup under trees.

I also ordered the 2-pack clips. These are nice because they come with an adapter on them. If you remove the threaded black female cylinder and threaded ring, you are left with a standard sized male mount that will fit a tripod base. You do not need to make a separate purchase for an adapter, it's already there. The ball joint swivels all the way around and there is a groove in the base to tilt the clip in towards the base, so you can use these clips for holding the reflectors, diffuser or even a backdrop on a side or top mount adapter of your backdrop frame.

Thank you for reading my review. I hope you found it helpful.
text_fidelity_b: 42 Inch/106CM Light Reflector 5-in-1 Collapsible Multi-Disc with Bag - Translucent, Silver, Gold, White and Black for Studio Photography Lighting and Outdoor Lighting

Ring Video Doorbell (1st Gen) – 720p HD video, motion activated alerts, easy installation – Satin Nickel The lifetime warranty on this doorbell is the real deal. This is a very well-supported doorbell.

I was having issues with holiday season package thieves and a non-working wireless doorbell. Ring is the only video doorbell I could find that will work wirelessly. The first one had battery issues. Replaced no problem. The second one had sound issues. Replaced no problem. The third on works FLAWLESSLY. I absolutely love it.

The smart motion sensor works well. I see everyone who comes onto my porch, but not my neighbors' porches (three doors lined up on one big house). Two way sound is mostly good -> if it's really windy, it's hard to hear sometimes. The video is way better than I thought it would be. I can see well enough on my phone, but if I download and watch on my computer, it is very impressive.

I signed up for the cloud recording - it's the least expensive pay service of any of my security cameras, and it has been reliable over the few weeks I have been using it. The doorbell is also conspicuous enough to act as a deterrent. I've had a couple of alerts where people looked like they were going to come up the steps and then changed their minds. Both my postal carrier and my UPS driver said that a lot of their stops have these, and they really like them.

Bottom line: It took a couple of tries, but I am one hundred percent happy with this doorbell. If you have an issue, use the warranty. It's a real thing.

UPDATE: I have a CHIME now, as well, and it also works beautifully. The Ring Company gave it to me for free as a promotion, because I had bought two of their doorbells.

Amazon Basics 67-Inch Monopod, Black The Amazon Basics 67-Inch Monopod is basically (pardon the pun) everything you need in a monopod. It extends to a nice height and even at full extension it feels reasonably sturdy. Collapsing the thinnest section and using just the two thicker sections increases the stability greatly and still gives you a little over 51 inches to work with.

Build quality is decent. The locking cams are hard plastic but don't feel cheap and give a positive, tight lock when engaged. The foam grip isn't glued into place. It is just held in place by friction and the three screw heads that hold the camera mount to the monopod.

The monopod also includes a wrist strap held in place on the head of the mount by a split ring.

A carry bag is supplied. It's enough to protect the monopod though it's not padded and the shoulder strap is short enough to be more of a carry strap.

The rubber foot of this monopod can be retracted on its threaded mount to expose a metal spike foot for use in outdoor.

The only negatives I've found with this monopod are:
The wrist strap is rather small and I cannot fit it over my hand. For reference I wear a size large glove. For me this is more of a palm strap.

The soft foot has very little rubber extending past the end of the metal spike. I measured this at just slightly over 1mm. Moderate wear will surely leave the metal foot expose and potentially damage flooring.

All in all though this is an affordable and well built monopod and I wouldn't hesitate to recommend it.
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Basics 67-Inch Monopod, Black

Cobra RX680 Waterproof Walkie Talkies for Adults - Rechargeable, 60 Preset Channels, Long Range 38-Mile Two-Way Radio Set (2-Pack),Black and Orange So many things I love about these. These appear to be as rugged and well built as I'd expected from a brand name like Cobra. I love that they include a flashlight, and especially that the units are USB rechargeable! Such a convenient way to power things these days, I wish more electronics ditched the AAA batteries thing like this!
The range might be a bit exaggerated, but to be fair I live in a very wooded area surrounded by hills and valleys. I found that around my neighborhood it worked great but if I went a few miles away, the sound was mostly just unintelligible crackling. We could still hear that someone was trying to say something, but that's it.
On the flip side, we started hearing someone else's conversation the next day... we were just testing it so we didn't bother changing the default channel, and it turns out someone else must have gotten some talkies on the same default frequencies. I have no idea how close they were, but my kids pointed out that someone was talking and we didn't press any buttons and then we all heard it. "Dad? Do I need to come in? I'm playing outside", and then a few seconds later "ok, but don't ride into the street". Then some clicks of singing and other noises- clearly someone else communicating with THEIR kid was coming through to us. I pressed the talk button and said "Hi- this is the default frequency for these walkie talkies, so we should both probably change them!" and then promptly picked another channel. So, that's kind of neat because I have no idea where these other people were, we live in a pretty urban area with houses spread out and I know it wasn't someone from my block. Yet we heard them clear as day. So, I'd say these are pretty good at what they do, but maybe don't rely on the full extent of their listed range.
text_fidelity_b: Cobra RX680 Waterproof Walkie Talkies for Adults - Rechargeable, 60 Preset Channels, Long Range 38-Mile Two-Way Radio Set (2-Pack),Black and Orange

I kept getting errors and it said it was read only blah, blah, blah. Needless to say I just stashed it because my family was going through a crisis and I didn't have the mental reserve to give this any attention.
Fast forward, I am cleaning out a drawer and found the drive again. I remembered it had issues but my spider senses said plug it into the USB on the Xbox 360 and it worked. text_fidelity_a:
Sony 4 GB Walkman Video MP3 Player (Pink) I had an iPod 2GB Nano and wanted to get something with larger capacity. I did some research and finally bought the Walkman. I was around for the very first Sony Walkman casette tape player, so the idea of getting a Sony MP3 player was appealing.
After using it for over a month, I find it a great little device. The battery life is amazing. I charged it over two weeks ago and have used it on multiple three hour car rides. I also had it hooked up to a speaker in my office and left it on for several hours and it stil has battery life.
It took me some time to get used to the navigation, but now I am fine with the difference between the Walkman and the iPod. The sound quality is good and although the volume could be better, it is acceptable for my use.
The major problem I have with the unit is the software. Sony included one of those mini disc's which loaded a couple of software programs on my computer. The main program is one which allows you to drag and drop files from your computer to the player; however, it doesn't work. I dragged a few tunes to see how it worked and then started dragging all the music. The software kept accepting the tunes, but after it "loaded" for about 2 hours, I discovered it had only loaded the first set of tunes. The rest, and the two hour wait, was for nothing. The software also has a "delete" function, which also doesn't work. It tells you that it delets items from the player, but they are still there.
So, I junked that software and decided to use the Windows Media Player. This is ok, except that the Media Player has a very odd way to create playlists. There are some round about ways to create the play list and I have finaly learned how to do it, but it took way too long compared to iTunes. The other odd thing is that when you create a play list it has to be from tunes on your computer, not on the device. Then when you sync the device to load the playlist, it may or may not put duplicate versions of the music on the device. Sometimes it finds the songs on the device and sometimes it does not. So, I ended up with multiple copies of some songs. The device software is also pathetic. It doesn't allow you to create playlists on the device, and as others have noted, there is no way to delete items from the device without using the software.
I finally just had the computer recognize the device as an external drive and was able to load songs and delete them with no probme.
Despite the isues, I still like the device better than my Nano. For one thing it has an FM receiver, which works great. Now that I have come to terms with the crappy software, it works great. So, if you are looking for an alternative to the iPod, this is a good option. Just stay away from the software provided by Sony and you will be fine.
text_fidelity_b: Sony 4 GB Walkman Video MP3 Player (Pink)
