text_fidelity_a:
Targus Vuscape Case and Stand for iPad mini (fits iPad mini 1, 2, 3) Black (THZ182US) The Targus VuScape Protective cover and stand is a pretty good, helpful aid for those who own an Apple Ipad2. It features a thin, lightweight design that is meant to hold the iPad2 snugly in place while you work.

Having a stand for your iPad is certainly a good idea and I like that this stand can be used to position your iPad in different ways. There are multiple grooves so that you can display your iPad at different angles. The cover can also be folded back completely, allowing the consumer to hold the iPad in the hands without the stand.

This protective cover/stand does have some nice features to offer, but after using it for a while, it is more than apparent that the stand is not perfect. Probably the greatest issue is that the stand isn't as sturdy as I would prefer. If you use the stand on a solid, flat surface, you shouldn't have too many problems, but place it on other surfaces and it tends to bend just a little bit. The slightest bend will cause the grooves to give way just a little, and the iPad will no longer be securely held in place.

I generally like the thin, lightweight design of this stand, but the thinness possibly goes a tad far. If the manufacturer had made this stand just a little bit thicker, it would be stronger and more likely to hold the iPad in place without any problems. I suppose this is the trade- off one must make when selecting a stand such as this. Lightweight is nice, especially for something like an iPad, but lightweight means the stand is lacking in strength.

All in all, this is a good stand and certainly worth considering, but not a deluxe stand like I expected. Again, as long as you are willing to sacrifice sturdiness for lightweight design, you should be fine. And try to use only on the flattest surfaces for the best results. Follow these guidelines and you should find yourself reasonably happy with this protective cover and stand from Targus.
text_fidelity_b: Targus Vuscape Case and Stand for iPad mini (fits iPad mini 1, 2, 3) Black (THZ182US)

text_fidelity_a:
Amazon Basics USB 3.1 Type-C to 4-Port Aluminum Hub Connector, Black One of the problems I have seen with the latest crop of notebooks and Ultrabooks that have come out is a lack of USB ports. There's usually a need for more ports than these systems have and it gets frustrating. A small USB hub like this is a good solution. That said, this particular hub does not have a separate power source so some consideration must be made when plugging in power-hungry devices.

From a design stantpoint this is a solid unit, shaped to be accessible without being huge. It has a little weight to it and this is helpful for keeping it stable. The addition of Velcro strips in the package to secure it in one place is a welcome inclusion and makes securing the hub very simple no matter what your configuration is.

The hub provides four USB 3.1 type A ports. Let me state what should be obvious - this will not convert a USB 1.1 or 2.0 port into a 3.1 port, so plug it into a 3.1 port if you want the speed across the hub. For my specific uses, it does not need to be a high-speed hub and I am find with using it as a 2.0 hub, but admittedly that's slightly wasteful.

There is no power port on this hub and there is no DC adapter in the box. So, any power that the hub needs comes through the onboard port into which it is plugged. That's fine for low-power devices like mice, keyboards, memory sticks and so on, but if the intent is to plug in such things as USB hard drives with no external power supply this can cause some headaches. No, one drive isn't going to overload the hub, but if you have multiple drives attached there may be reliability issues when they starve one another for power. When the device plugged in has its own power supply (like a big backup drive), this has little impact on the hub.

The point is, plan carefully how you intend to use the hub.

I like this hub and it does a good job for what it is. It has given me three extra ports on an Ultrabook I use which is all I could ask for. The ability to power this hub with it's own power supply would be the only area for improvement I could find.
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Basics USB 3.1 Type-C to 4-Port Aluminum Hub Connector, Black

text_fidelity_a: GOgroove FlexSMART X2 Mini Bluetooth FM Transmitter Radio Adapter Car Kit, USB Charging, Hands Free Calling, Music Controls, AUX Input – Compatible with MP3 Players, iPhone, Samsung, and More Devices I've gone through a couple FM transmitters, and all have had problems with static noise, even on the best stations. I was skeptical at first about the GOgroove FlexSMART since it was above the amount I was expecting to spend and I had been disappointed by my previous other transmitters. I read the reviews and decided to give it a try because I was sick of constantly adjusting the device so I could just hear some clear music. The GOgroove worked perfectly the very first time I used it. I was very impressed. Where other transmitters were horrible quality on almost all stations, it's the exact opposite with this one (nearly all stations are good/great quality). The arm it uses is really secure and easy to bend. Controls are easy and don't require you to look at in order to use them. Comes with all needed cables.  On top of all that, it has a USB port, can be used for hands free calling, and charges your device! But most importantly, THE SOUND QUALITY IS EXCELLENT! I would say this is totally worth the extra bucks because you won't need to get another one anytime soon.
